stand: South Korea and the US-led UN Command have concluded North Korea planted four mines, laid about a year before the blast, wounding three soldiers in the DMZ on 21 September. Seoul demands an apology, has cleared mines on its side, and its civilian leadership has called for dialogue. Pyongyang, through Kim Yo Jong, denies crossing the line, has rejected Seoul's medical aid as a "politically motivated scheme", and demands Seoul show "utmost respect" before ties can be restored; its Foreign Ministry warns it will meet any Southern incursion with force.

claims.text: North Korea planted the mines that caused the 21 Sep DMZ blast.
claims.by: Says: South Korea's military and the US-led UN Command, after joint investigation. Denies: North Korea.

claims.text: At least four mines, including one unexploded, were found at the blast site.
claims.by: Says: South Korean military and UN Command investigation.

claims.text: North Korean soldiers crossed the Military Demarcation Line.
claims.by: Says: South Korean military. Denies: Kim Yo Jong, North Korea.

claims.text: The mine placement violated the 1953 Armistice Agreement.
South Korea demands a formal apology from North Korea; Pyongyang has refused.
claims.by: Says: South Korea's military. Refuses: North Korea, with Kim Yo Jong calling the demand "despicable".

claims.text: North Korea rejected Seoul's proposal to jointly resurvey the MDL, saying it will fix its border by force.
claims.by: Says: Unification Minister Chung Dong-young proposed the resurvey. Denies/rejects: Kim Yo Jong.

claims.text: North Korea's Foreign Ministry states it will use force against any Southern military incursion.
claims.by: Says: North Korea's Foreign Ministry (KCNA statement, reported by TASS).

claims.text: South Korea has begun clearing mines on its side of the MDL.
The mines were planted by North Korean forces about a year before the blast, not shortly before it.
North Korea demands South Korea show utmost respect before ties can be restored.
Seoul's civilian leadership has called on North Korea to return to dialogue, apart from the military's apology demand.
claims.by: Says: CNA report, citing Seoul's civilian leadership.

timeline.text: Two mines exploded in the DMZ, injuring three South Korean soldiers, two seriously.
South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff gave a preliminary assessment blaming North Korean mines.
Kim Yo Jong denied North Korean soldiers crossed the border, calling the incident a farce.
Unification Minister Chung Dong-young proposed a joint resurvey of the MDL.
Kim Yo Jong rejected the resurvey proposal, saying the border will be set by force.
South Korea's military announced final investigation results naming North Korea responsible and demanded an apology.
South Korea's military carried out a mine-clearing operation at the blast site.
North Korea's Foreign Ministry warned it would use force against any Southern military incursion.
Seoul said it was not ruling out measures to force an apology from Pyongyang.
Defence Minister Kang Shin-chul called the military's response unprecedented and said all responsibility lies with North Korea.
Foreign Minister Cho Hyun said Seoul was considering various diplomatic measures over the incident.
Kim Yo Jong rejected South Korea's medical aid offer, calling it a politically motivated scheme.
Kim Yo Jong said Seoul must show utmost respect, consideration and sincerity to mend ties.
